reviews.body: The citations_delta handling looks consistent with the existing SDK-accumulated block lifecycle; I found no blocking code defect in this patch. Please rebase onto current main, resolve the merge conflicts and run CI. An end-to-end assertion that the final response retains its citations would strengthen the current no-exception test.

Thanks, this addresses my earlier review. Main is merged and the end-to-end test is there.

Verified:
- `lib/active_agent/providers/anthropic_provider.rb:225` matches the existing `input_json_delta` handling. Citations aren't lost: `content_block_stop` replaces the block with the gem's accumulated `content_block`, and `message_stop` replaces the whole message. Both carry `citations`, so streaming now agrees with the non-streaming path.
- `test/providers/anthropic/streaming_citations_test.rb` streams a real SSE body through the gem's accumulator and asserts `cited_text`/`document_title` on the final message, which checks preservation and not only that nothing raised.
- Merges cleanly with main, and the CHANGELOG entry is under Unreleased.

Non-blocking:
1. CI hasn't reported on this head yet; the fork workflows need a maintainer's approval to run. This approval assumes they come back green.
2. `response.message` doesn't expose citations, streamed or not. A follow-up to surface them at the agent level would be worthwhile.
3. #594 also adds a `### Fixed` heading under Unreleased, so whichever merges second will get a small CHANGELOG conflict.

comments.body:
Merged current main (the only conflict was CHANGELOG.md; both entries kept) and added an end-to-end test, `test/providers/anthropic/streaming_citations_test.rb`. It streams a cited answer over the Messages wire format (WebMock SSE, through the anthropic gem's stream accumulation): a `citations_delta` arrives before the text, and the test checks that the final message handed to the stream broadcaster at close still has the text block's citation (`cited_text`, `document_title`). The test fails with `Unexpected delta type: citations_delta` without the fix.

One note: the common `Messages::Assistant` in `response.message` carries only role and text, so citations aren't exposed on the agent-level response, streamed or not. The test asserts at the provider message level for that reason.

`bin/test` with Ruby 3.4.11 and `gemfiles/rails8.gemfile` on the merged branch: 3883 runs, 1 failure, `LocalSandboxBackendTest#test_an_exception_raised_into_a_boot_stops_the_setup_step_it_interrupted`. The same test fails on main's latest CI run (`test (3.4, gemfiles/rails8.gemfile)`). The new test file passes on its own and passes rubocop.
